To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
computer anxiety and the belief about usefulness of computer technology were associated with effective use of computer in general practice.
the use of computers in general practice is associated with a number of demographic factors, including gender, age, and type of practice (solo vs group), and with attitudes to the technology.

(1) GPs' attitudes towards the use of computers are associated with their effective use of computers for clinical functions; (2) female GPs are more likely than male GPs to effectively use computers for clinical functions, while those working in partnership or groups are also more likely to effectively use computers than those in solo practice; and (3) GPs who are more confident in their use of computers are more likely to use them effectively for clinical functions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how attitudes to computers and the practice environment influence effective computer use by GPs in Australian general practice.
the use of computer technology in general practice, and in particular, the use of computers for clinical purposes.
the role of attitude in computer use among Australian GPs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the attitude of a practitioner is the most important factor in the effective use of computer technology in clinical functions in general medical practice.
GPs who are less anxious about computer use are more likely to use computers in clinical practice.
GPs who are more confident and comfortable with computers are more likely to use them effectively.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the more GPs believe in the usefulness of computers, the more likely they are to use computers for clinical functions.
GPs with high levels of computer anxiety are less likely to use computers in practice.
the attitude of GPs is a key factor in effective use of computers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
GPs who are more anxious about using computers are less likely to use computers for clinical functions.
the use of computers for clinical functions in general practice is still not universal.
the use of computer technology by GPs is not just about having the right hardware and software.
